purpose: State the exact finite proposition needed to transfer Gaffke validity to an affine ordered-sample upper bound, without embedding any proof data.

inputs.tail_probability: alpha in a declared subset of (0,1)
inputs.factors: upper Clopper-Pearson roots p_n(0),...,p_n(n), with p_n(n)=1

target: For every declared alpha and every normalized ordered knot vector, P(sum_{k=1}^{n-1} z_k D_k + D_n > s) <= alpha.
transfer_rule: The target implies pointwise domination of the finite-sample-valid Gaffke bounded-mean upper limit and hence coverage at least 1-alpha for every i.i.d. distribution on [0,1].

verification_obligations.statement: Enclose every factor over the complete declared alpha domain and prove every factor ordering or algebraic identity used.
Partition the complete ordered-knot simplex by the position of s among the knots, including all boundary faces.

Derive the uniform-Dirichlet cap expressions and reduce the target either directly to residual signs or to an exact section derivative plus local step-cap barriers; clear only denominators whose signs are proved.
Give a fixed oriented simplex chain whose support is exactly each polynomial region, with boundary cancellation, or an equivalent exact maximum/face-induction argument.
Prove every omitted Bernstein coefficient vanishes identically on the declared factor locus or boundary face.
Prove every remaining coefficient in every residual used by the selected direct or face-induction route nonnegative by exact arithmetic or outward-rounded enclosures.
Transfer the inequalities to repeated-knot faces by direct formulas or continuity.
Expose the complete finite sign statement and enough deterministic inputs to regenerate it.

instances.arithmetic_requirement: exact rational arithmetic and rigorously enclosed binary64 Bernstein arithmetic with exact rational forward-error bounds
exact symbolic identities and integer-directed dyadic interval arithmetic
exact symbolic identities and outward-rounded Arb real-ball arithmetic

non_goals: No claim is made for alpha values or sample sizes outside an instance's declared domain.
No ordinary all-sample-size Stringer theorem follows from the interface alone.
No finite-population or sampling-without-replacement design bridge is included.
